# Load libraries and data
```{r}
library(tidyverse)

theme_set(theme_bw())
`%notin%` <- Negate(`%in%`)


res.lipid <- read.csv("C:/Users/patri/python_workspace/copepods-lipid-content/prediction_outputs/loki2013_lipid/prediction_results_lipid.csv")

res.lipid.crop <- read.csv("C:/Users/patri/python_workspace/copepods-lipid-content/prediction_outputs/loki2013_lipid_pcrop/prediction_results_lipid_pcrop.csv")

res.prosome <- read.csv("C:/Users/patri/python_workspace/copepods-lipid-content/prediction_outputs/loki2013_prosome/prediction_results_prosome.csv")

meta.testrain <- read.csv("C:/Users/patri/python_workspace/data_loki/dataset_split_lipid_prosomecrop.csv")

res.lipid <- res.lipid %>% 
  left_join(meta.testrain, by = "filename")
res.lipid.crop <- res.lipid.crop %>% 
  left_join(meta.testrain, by = "filename")
res.prosome <- res.prosome %>% 
  left_join(meta.testrain, by = "filename")
```

# Train vs Test data

## Prosome results
- compare pixels, axes
- plot size/pixels vs accuracy
- separate test and train
```{r}
# Summary stats
res.prosome %>% 
  filter(prosome_pixels_predicted != 0) %>% 
  group_by(split) %>% 
  summarise(n = n(),
            IoU.mean = mean(IoU),
            IoU.median = median(IoU),
            Recall.mean = mean(Recall),
            F1score.mean = mean(F1score),
            .groups = "drop")


cowplot::plot_grid(
  ggplot(res.prosome, aes(x = prosome_pixels_annotated,
                          y = prosome_pixels_predicted,
                          color = split)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
    theme(legend.position = "none") +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
    geom_abline(),
  
  ggplot(res.prosome, aes(x = prosome_pixels_annotated,
                          y = IoU,
                          color = split)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
    geom_smooth() +
    theme(legend.position = "none") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 80, linetype = "dashed", color = "orange") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 90, linetype = "longdash", color = "orange"),
  
  
  ggplot(res.prosome, aes(x = prosome_pixels_annotated,
                          y = F1score,
                          color = split)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
    geom_smooth() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 80, linetype = "dashed", color = "orange") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 90, linetype = "longdash", color = "orange"),
  
  
  ggplot(res.prosome, aes(x = prosome_pixels_annotated,
                          y = Recall,
                          color = split)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
    geom_smooth() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 80, linetype = "dashed", color = "orange") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 90, linetype = "longdash", color = "orange"),
  rel_heights = c(1,1.2)
)

ggsave("figures/LOKI2013_prosome_accuracy.png",
       heigh = 5, width = 7, units = "in")
```

## Lipids results
### Compare cropped prosome vs original image
```{r, eval=FALSE}
res.lipid %>% 
  group_by(split) %>% 
  summarise(n = n(),
            IoU.mean = mean(IoU),
            IoU.median = median(IoU),
            Recall.mean = mean(Recall),
            F1score.mean = mean(F1score, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")
res.lipid.crop %>% 
  group_by(split) %>% 
  summarise(n = n(),
            IoU.mean = mean(IoU),
            IoU.median = median(IoU),
            Recall.mean = mean(Recall),
            F1score.mean = mean(F1score, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

# Compare metrics for with cropped prosome or not
comp.lipids <- res.lipid %>% 
  mutate(model = "original image") %>% 
  # pivot_longer(cols = lipid_pixels_annotated:F1score,
  #              names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>% 
  left_join(res.lipid.crop %>% 
              mutate(model = "cropped prosome"),
            by = join_by(filename, split),
            suffix = c(" no crop"," with crop")) %>% 
  rename("lipid annotated no crop" = "lipid_pixels_annotated no crop",
         "lipid predicted no crop" = "lipid_pixels_predicted no crop",
         "lipid annotated with crop" = "lipid_pixels_annotated with crop",
         "lipid predicted with crop" = "lipid_pixels_predicted with crop")

# Model performance is OFTEN (but not always) better when prosome is cropped. The cropped-prosome model can perform really well even when the original image model has poor performance
cowplot::plot_grid(
  ggplot(comp.lipids, aes(x = `lipid predicted no crop`, 
                          y = `lipid predicted with crop`, color = split)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
    theme(legend.position = "none") +
    geom_abline(),
  
  ggplot(comp.lipids, aes(x = `IoU no crop`, y = `IoU with crop`, color = split)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
    theme(legend.position = "none") +
    geom_abline(),
  
  ggplot(comp.lipids, aes(x = `Recall no crop`, y = `Recall with crop`, color = split)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
    geom_abline(),
  
  ggplot(comp.lipids, aes(x = `F1score no crop`, y = `F1score with crop`, color = split)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
    geom_abline(),
  rel_heights = c(1,1.2)
)


ggsave("figures/LOKI2013_prosome_crop_comparison.png",
       heigh = 5, width = 7, units = "in")

# rm(comp.lipids)
# rm(res.lipid)
```

## Combine prosome and lipid, calculate fullness and plot distributions
```{r}
res.lf <- res.lipid.crop %>% 
  select(filename, lipid_pixels_annotated:lipid_pixels_predicted) %>% 
  left_join(select(res.prosome,
                   filename, prosome_pixels_annotated,
                   prosome_pixels_predicted),
            by = join_by(filename)) %>% 
  mutate(lipidfullness_annotated = lipid_pixels_annotated/prosome_pixels_annotated*100,
         lipidfullness_predicted = lipid_pixels_predicted/prosome_pixels_predicted*100) %>% 
  mutate(object_id = str_remove(filename,".png"))


ggplot(res.lf, aes(x = lipid_pixels_annotated, y = prosome_pixels_annotated)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth()

ggplot(res.lf, aes(x = lipid_pixels_annotated, y = lipidfullness_annotated)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth()

ggplot(res.lf %>% 
         filter(lipidfullness_predicted < 100), aes(x = lipid_pixels_predicted, 
                                                    y = lipidfullness_predicted)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth()



ggplot(res.lf, aes(x = lipid_pixels_annotated, y = lipid_pixels_predicted)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth() +
  geom_abline()

ggplot(res.lf, aes(x = prosome_pixels_annotated, y = prosome_pixels_predicted)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth() +
  geom_abline()

# TODO Why is the predicted lipid fullness a bad fit when the predicted pixels are good? Because predicted prosome is slightly larger and predicted lipids slightly smaller??
ggplot(res.lf %>% 
         filter(lipidfullness_predicted < 100), aes(x = lipidfullness_annotated, 
                                                    y = lipidfullness_predicted)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth() +
  geom_abline()
```



# Matching LOKI metadata
Note that only 4 dates were used in the LOKI 2013 lipid sementations, (2013-08-15, 2013-08-16, 2013-08-18, 2013-09-02)
```{r, eval=FALSE}
load("data/LOKI2013_metadata.RData"))
`%notin%` <- Negate(`%in%`)

# The list of images used in the prosome and lipid segmentation
meta.testrain <- meta.testrain %>% 
  mutate(object_id = str_remove(filename, ".bmp"))

# ** Both the JPR paper metadata and the Loki-copepod lipids ecotaxa project retain the longitude, latitude, and depth inforation that are found in the ArcticNet_2013 project

# Only copepods with visible lipid sac (subset for prosome segmentation?)
# This is a smaller set of images than those used in the JPR paper and even a smaller subset of images with segmented prosomes
lokiLipid <- read.table("../../Laval-imaging-analysis/LOKI_for_prosome_segmentation/ecotaxa_export_2331_20250331_1834.tsv", sep = '\t', header = TRUE)

# # Actually the JPR paper uses 2216 images which are list in this file. These will exactly match the object_ids of the files used in the segmentation
# lokiJPR <- read.table("data/ecotaxa_table_JPR-2023-061.tsv",
#                    sep = "\t", header = TRUE)
# lokiJPR <- lokiJPR[-1,]

AA <- lokiLipid %>% 
  filter(object_id %in% meta.testrain$object_id)


# 
# # The LOKI_ArcticNet_2013 project data (takes a long time to open)
# meta <- read.csv("C:/Users/patri/Downloads/export_12063_20250122_1820/ecotaxa_export_12063_20250122_1820.tsv",
#                  sep = '\t', header = TRUE)

meta <- meta %>% 
  mutate(object_id = str_squish(object_id))

metasub <- meta %>% 
  filter(object_date %in% unique(lokiLipid$object_date)) %>% 
  select(object_id:object_time) %>% 
# sample_id is the first three segments of object_id
  mutate(sample_id = str_sub(object_id, start = 1, end = 19)) %>% 
  mutate(sample_id2 = str_sub(object_id, start = 1, end = 15))

# Only 581 images have a direct match with the ArcticNet2013 metadata
zz <- meta %>% 
  filter(object_id %in% lokiLipid$object_id)

# List the images in the JPR analysis with no clear metadata
# Matching by object_date, object_time, and sample_id does not work and even the 12 supposed matches have wrong object_ids
loki_tofind <- lokiLipid %>% 
  filter(object_id %notin% metasub$object_id) %>% 
  select(object_id_tofind = object_id,
         object_date, object_time, sample_id, sample_cruise, sample_stationid) %>% 
  mutate(sample_id2 = str_sub(object_id_tofind, start = 1, end = 15)) %>% 
  left_join(metasub,
            by = join_by(object_date, object_time, sample_id2)) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(object_lon))

# Most samples occured on the same date so object_data is not effective alone. Matching by both object_date and object_time also is not effective since many WRONG sample_id matches are linked to the same object_data and object_time.
loki_tofind2 <- lokiLipid %>% 
  filter(object_id %notin% metasub$object_id) %>% 
  select(object_id_tofind = object_id,
         object_date, object_time, sample_id, sample_cruise, sample_stationid) %>% 
  left_join(metasub,
            by = join_by(object_date, object_time))

# save(meta, lokiLipid, file = "data/LOKI2013_metadata.RData")
```
